haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices to the shadow store, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing its invoices into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person sets billing_mode to both; the controller refuses if the gate fails.
haiku-low.q4: The new engine's charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window starts automatic rollback. This happens only in both or new_only, never shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To move forward again, a person sets shadow with no gate; the 7-day count restarts and Finance sign-off must be given again.
haiku-low.q6: From day 35 onward in new_only, rollback is refused. The old engine stopped computing at new_only entry, and its skipped usage events age out of the 35-day log.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is kept in comparison_results. The controller refuses any forward move unless its gate has passed, and billing_mode lives in the config service.
haiku-low.q9: Component: NOT STATED. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate; above 2% over any 10-minute window, it starts an automatic rollback.
haiku-low.q10: Pause_charging stops the new engine's charges during rollback. The old engine charges again only at resume_charging, after reconcile finishes. Charges falling due during the pause: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile checks the ledger before each charge, so reruns cannot double-charge. It charges only the shadow-store amount minus existing ledger charges, once.
haiku-low.q12: Charging stays paused, the record shows the failed step, and no later step runs. The runner retries automatically, skipping done steps; on-call is alerted at first failure.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store (never charged, never written to the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing invoices into the shadow store, without charging, so it stays current.
sonnet.q3: The gate must pass: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person sets billing_mode to both; the controller refuses if the gate has not passed.
sonnet.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window starts an automatic rollback. It applies in both and new_only only; shadow errors never start one.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To go forward again, a person sets shadow (no gate), then the gates restart: the 7-day count resets to zero and Finance sign-off must be given again. Old comparison_results rows don't count.
sonnet.q6: On day 35 in new_only (day 35 or later, rollback is refused). The old engine stopped computing when new_only began, and its skipped usage events age out of the 35-day usage event log, so catch_up can no longer work.
sonnet.q8: The evidence is in comparison_results (nightly job rows with totals and mismatch flags); for both to new_only, Finance sign-off is also needed. The controller refuses a forward move unless its gate has passed, and it never moves on its own; a person sets the mode.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. The document says the condition is the new engine's charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window (denominator unclear) in both or new_only, and when met an automatic rollback starts.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED. The document only says pause_charging stops the new engine's charges and resume_charging (the old engine charges again) runs only after reconcile has finished. How charges falling due are handled in between is not stated.
sonnet.q11: Reconcile charges only the difference between the amount due (old engine's invoice in the shadow store) and the amount already charged (sum of ledger charges for the period), once. It checks the ledger before each charge, so a rerun cannot charge twice.
sonnet.q12: Charging stays paused, the rollback record shows the step, on-call is alerted, and the runner automatically retries the step. No later step runs. Done steps are skipped on retry; steps are safe to run twice. If retries run out, on-call takes over with charging still paused.
